findings.title: HISTORICAL: HuBERT audio-classification built and perfed on CPU at L0 effort
findings.observation: xbgoose/hubert-large-speech-emotion-recognition-russian-dusha-finetuned exported and ran with zero recipe customization. Export produced 1150 nodes optimized to 771 nodes (13 unique op types). Input shape [1, 16000] float32 (1s of 16kHz audio). Both fp32 and fp16 passed build+perf on cpu/cpu. Analyze confirmed full accelerator support on NvTensorRTRTX, QNN, and OpenVINO EPs.

falsified_on: xbgoose/hubert-large-speech-emotion-recognition-russian-dusha-finetuned@2eaa20433d7e6d5be7587b5f9f0057527ed274ba @ Transformers 5.14.1 requires export.compatibility.transformers_attention=eager in the refreshed FP32/FP16 recipes; see hubert-002

gotchas: fp16 on CPU is slower than fp32 — expected behavior due to CPU upcasting fp16→fp32 at runtime, not a defect
findings.mechanism_notes: CPU fp16 slowdown is well-known ORT behavior: CPU EP lacks native fp16 compute, upcasts every op. Would be falsified if a future ORT version adds CPU fp16 kernels.

findings.title: Transformers 5 HuBERT CPU recipes need eager attention metadata and preserve FP32/FP16 parity without an FP16 CPU speedup
findings.observation: Candidate e2667d973ca9f55437f8a5604d3ee2b4b42ba8f3 refreshed both exact CPU recipes for xbgoose/hubert-large-speech-emotion-recognition-russian-dusha-finetuned@2eaa20433d7e6d5be7587b5f9f0057527ed274ba by adding export.compatibility.transformers_attention=eager. On winml 0.3.0, Transformers 5.14.1, PyTorch 2.13.0, and onnxruntime-windowsml 1.24.5.202604171637, resolved configs also enabled gelu_fusion and matmul_add_fusion. HTP export identified HubertForSequenceClassification with 315,702,405 parameters, 409 modules, 118 traced modules, and 236 execution steps. FP32 produced 771 nodes, 420 FLOAT plus 11 INT64 initializers, and 1,262,802,308 external-data bytes; FP16 produced 773 nodes, 420 FLOAT16 plus 11 INT64 initializers, preserved FP32 I/O, and 631,400,642 bytes. CPU perf was FP32 mean/P50/P90 137.563/135.837/144.559 ms at 7.27 samples/s and +90.66 MB inference RSS, versus FP16 167.434/165.904/179.107 ms at 5.97 samples/s and +43.36 MB. Identical named-input PyTorch parity passed: FP32 cosine 1.0 and max-abs 1.0133e-05; FP16 cosine 0.9999966 and max-abs 0.0115724. Static Analyze counted 771 ops/13 types for FP32 and 773 ops/14 types for FP16; populated NvTensorRTRTX, QNN, and OpenVINO rule rows classified every present op supported, but these are not accelerator runtime verdicts.

not_yet_tested_on: Actual NvTensorRTRTX, QNN, OpenVINO, DML, CUDA, MIGraphX, TensorRT, or VitisAI runtime execution
W8A8 or W8A16 on any execution provider

findings.effort_tier_required: L0 (recipe refresh only; current toolchain requires explicit eager-attention compatibility metadata)
findings.goal_tier_reached: L0/L1/L2 PASS for cpu/cpu/fp32 and cpu/cpu/fp16; L3 FP32 CPU evidence is recorded separately in hubert-004
gotchas: Regenerate historical HuBERT recipes under Transformers 5 with export.compatibility.transformers_attention=eager; the accepted candidate changes only that JSON pointer in each recipe.
Build FP16 with explicit --precision fp16 and verify 420 FLOAT16 initializers plus the approximately 0.5 external-data size ratio; recipe naming alone does not prove realized precision.
FP16 halved external weights and reduced measured inference RSS but was slower than FP32 on this CPU; do not claim a CPU latency improvement.
The optimized component join mapped 517 nodes and retained 254 FP32 / 256 FP16 generated-name gaps explicitly; do not infer missing lineage or promote static rule coverage to runtime support.
findings.mechanism_notes: Exact recipe-authority builds, resolved configs, initializer/size inspection, CPU perf, identical-input PyTorch parity, and complete 12-row static Analyze JSON were independently reproduced from the candidate. The eager-attention requirement is toolchain-era specific; non-CPU execution remains untested.

findings.title: The Russian DUSHA checkpoint uses an exact five-label mapping that must not inherit the upstream four-class enum
findings.observation: The pinned checkpoint config maps exactly neutral=0, angry=1, positive=2, sad=3, and other=4. The pinned DUSHA paper defines neutral as calm or still voice with no expressed emotion regardless of text sentiment; angry as anger or annoyance including yelling, gritted-teeth speech, or negative emphasis; positive as smile, laughter, admiration, playful tone, or positive emphasis; sad as sadness, melancholy, or a faded voice; and other as too-quiet, hissing/rattling, or no-voice recordings. The upstream four-class baseline enum instead uses angry=0, sad=1, neutral=2, positive=3 and excludes other, so it cannot determine this checkpoint's IDs. Candidate e2667d9 used an explicit exact-string mapping to checkpoint IDs, with no synonym, translation, case-folding, positional, or inferred mapping.

falsified_on: Using the DUSHA four-class baseline enum angry=0, sad=1, neutral=2, positive=3 for this five-class checkpoint
Inferring checkpoint IDs by source order, translation, synonym matching, or case folding
not_yet_tested_on: Other HuBERT emotion checkpoints or DUSHA-derived checkpoints with different id2label metadata

findings.effort_tier_required: L0 model recipe on the exact PR #1329 scalar-string evaluator dependency
findings.goal_tier_reached: L3 functional smoke PASS on FP32 CPU after complete atomic label prevalidation
gotchas: Treat checkpoint id2label as the ID authority and the pinned DUSHA paper as the meaning authority; neither source alone authorizes remapping.
The exact scalar-string mapping must be complete and prevalidated before inference: neutral->0, angry->1, positive->2, sad->3, other->4.
The other class is part of the checkpoint contract and includes unusable/no-voice audio; do not silently drop it to match the upstream four-class experiment.
findings.mechanism_notes: The pinned checkpoint config, paper semantics, explicit mapping artifact, scalar-string compatibility suite, and five represented source labels establish this exact mapping. A different checkpoint revision with changed id2label must be revalidated rather than inheriting these IDs.
findings.resolution: Validated through the PR #1329 scalar-string mapping path contained by candidate e2667d973ca9f55437f8a5604d3ee2b4b42ba8f3.

findings.title: The fixed one-second HuBERT graph supports a five-row functional smoke only under explicit single-window accounting
findings.observation: The checkpoint feature extractor expects normalized mono 16 kHz waveform audio and its model card allows padding/truncation to 160,000 samples (10 seconds), but the exported ONNX contract is fixed input_values float32[1,16000] to logits float32[1,5]. The accepted FP32 CPU Eval decoded with SoundFile, downmixed stereo, resampled to 16 kHz, truncated long clips to the first 16,000 samples, right-padded short clips, and ran exactly one forward for each of five selected rows with no multi-window fan-out. Requested/selected/processed/rejected were 5/5/5/0, all five checkpoint classes were represented, accuracy was 0.2, and represented-class macro-F1 was 0.08. This proves evaluator, preprocessing, mapping, and inference operability only; five hand-selected rows cannot support checkpoint-quality or population-accuracy claims.

falsified_on: Reporting the 5-row accuracy=0.2 or macro-F1=0.08 as representative checkpoint quality or a DUSHA benchmark
not_yet_tested_on: FP16 Eval or any non-CPU Eval tuple; L3 is the single final-SHA FP32 CPU functional smoke
Full ten-second model-card windows, multi-window utterance aggregation, or population-scale DUSHA metrics

findings.title: All five selected DUSHA smoke inputs are byte-identical official crowd_test members with zero podcast overlap
findings.observation: The five selected xbgoose/dusha@e3e309de7723f4dc4a0230b4b9d725061d561044 WAVs were streamed against the official DUSHA crowd.tar and matched exact crowd_test/wavs members byte-for-byte: neutral row 0 ada344669196aa8b9af02695f032c75804cbfbcee53b270253e92715529939d9, sad row 1 85adceb46c2615ee737d4ab451f85738fc46e8cb509f870df640e5787705823e, angry row 6 15d1dc08596911609578a2e5ed1b7170f51acdb4eddd7de7c6efaef28e05655b, positive row 7 36588ebcc27a35acf1fb0af3b0e4a8fc2238214285b40f856d4b2221f37dd8aa, and other row 20 e7f360a4ee07d28453ad8420d39ebb5520f43970ab2a716465de2b0797a21e3c. Official paper_setups crowd_test.jsonl and dusha_test.jsonl are byte-identical (SHA-256 7537ee08ffce93e3c059faae8a1cbf25d659347fbfdb1114a86ea12252da6b2), while podcast_test.jsonl has SHA-256 6cafef6df4e141c7c0af4bc164d4a3e2ec9f3c421c73bbdf302136f5d3251897 and overlaps none of the selected rows. The pinned upstream distribution statement says Crowd audio is directly distributed, whereas Podcast audio is withheld because of a license issue. Official English license text grants worldwide, royalty-free, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive, irrevocable reproduction and making-available rights subject to retained attribution/notices, modification indication, no endorsement, and no additional restrictive terms; the public bundle retained attribution and stated that audio was unmodified.
